title: Geologic Time: Then and Now
learningObjectives: Order key developments in understanding geologic time from Steno's laws to early radiometric dating
Explain how stratigraphic principles and uniformitarianism support relative age ordering
Describe how discovery of radioactivity and half-life dating revised Earth's age estimates

explanations.text: Geologic time spans billions of years, far beyond human experience, requiring tools that order events relatively and measure them numerically.

evidence.quote: Earth is 4.54 billion years old, a span of time that is hard for many people to grasp.

explanations.text: Early geologists ordered rock layers using superposition, original horizontality, and faunal succession, and Hutton argued present processes explain past deposits.

evidence.quote: The law of superposition says that older rocks are on the bottom and younger rocks are on the top.
In 1788, James Hutton proposed what would become the foundational principle of geology — uniformitarianism.

explanations.text: Radioactivity gave a heat source and a clock; later work dated meteorites and refined the geologic time scale with sensitive instruments.

evidence.quote: It was the discovery of radioactivity in 1896 that changed the heat-flow picture dramatically.
A half-life is the length of time it takes for half of the number of original, or parent, isotopes to decay to a stable daughter isotope.
Nicholas Steno, 1669, gets credit for first writing down basic geological principles as laws.
In 1788, James Hutton proposed what would become the foundational principle of geology — uniformitarianism.
The first geologic time scale was published in 1841 — Powell certainly would have known of it and used it in his geologic trips to the West.
It was the discovery of radioactivity in 1896 that changed the heat-flow picture dramatically.

events.label: Holmes calculates age by radiometric dating

evidence.quote: English geologist Arthur Holmes in 1913 calculated an age of 1.6 billion years, the first such estimate based on radiometric dating.

scenario.settingLabel: From Steno to Early Radiometric Dating
